actionCatalog.description: One of the seven voluntarily-adjusting members proposes or supports the monthly required-production decision: raise, hold, or reverse, effective the following month, with consent of the group's monthly meeting process. No monetary cost; decision effective for 30 days.

Vote at the 42nd ONOMM (29 November 2026) on adopting the 2027 MSC-based baselines or deferring them, and on the treatment of the wider-alliance cut layer. Motion carries by simple majority of the seven adjusters; no monetary cost.
Submit outstanding MSC assessment data to the Secretariat, advancing assessment completeness. Costs administrative effort from the actor's fiscal account over 14 days.
Secretariat tables the completed MSC assessment for the 42nd ONOMM when data completeness permits; only a tabled assessment enables the baseline vote. No monetary cost.
Set own actual crude output relative to the required level for the coming month; values above quota may trigger compliance consequences in the MOMR record. No monetary cost; effective 30 days.
UAE, outside the quota framework since its exit, sets its production level toward its stated capacity ceiling, adding supply outside any OPEC+ decision. No monetary cost; effective 30 days.
Deliver a month of compensation cuts against the outstanding schedule, reducing fiscal account through foregone revenue and raising the delivered-compensation metric. Takes 30 days.
Publish a monthly demand, supply and compliance assessment (OMR, MOMR or STEO) with a textual narrative visible to all actors. No monetary cost; published same day.
Issue a public statement or diplomatic signal on quotas, baselines, compensation or the disruption. No monetary cost; same day.
Saudi Arabia surges crude output above recent levels for a month (crisis supply), boosting the fiscal account via revenue at prevailing prices; cost is abstract operational draw. 30 days.
Hold position and take no action for a number of days.

assumptions.description: Fiscal accounts are abstract bargaining-resource stocks (index units), not observed budgets; initial balances are invented starting points with no claimed source.
Brent monthly mean initialises at 114.16 USD/bbl for September 2026 (EIA/FRED reported value; carried here under a scenario assumption because claim text carries no typed numeric qualifier).
MSC assessment completeness starts at 60 of 100 with data submissions outstanding; threshold to table is assumed at 90 by mid-November 2026.
Compensation delivery is initially undocumented and set to zero delivered; each delivered month adds 150 kb/d-months at an abstract revenue cost of 40 per action.
Kazakhstan's Q3 2026 over/under-quota gap is unknown and remains null until a compliance reading occurs.
Iraq's output-vs-quota gap initialises at -550 kb/d (under quota) per the IEA September 2026 reading; carried as an assumption because claim text carries no typed numeric qualifier.
Gulf shut-in supply initialises at 4.8 mb/d (September 2026 EIA estimate) and evolves via restoration actions and scheduled events.
UAE output initialises at 3.8 mb/d (June 2026 Reuters-sourced rebound) pending its ramp decisions.
Policy state as of mid-October 2026: monthly levels held at September 2026 values, 2022-era cut layer in force until 31 December 2026, 2027 baselines pending.

Initial relations mirror the researched alignment structure (Saudi-Russia partnership, UAE-Saudi rivalry, Secretariat monitoring of Kazakhstan, IEA-OPEC narrative conflict, Iraq lobbying, EIA-IEA alignment).
Monthly quota decisions are group policy acts by the seven adjusters; the decision value is the aggregate adjustment in kb/d, bounded at +/-700 kb/d.
The 42nd ONOMM baseline decision is modelled as a simple-majority vote of the seven adjusters with threshold 4 votes; outcome categories are adopt-modest, adopt-large or defer.

Each MSC data submission advances completeness by 15 points at an administrative cost of 10 from the submitting actor's account over 14 days; the Secretariat can table the assessment once completeness is high.
Members set actual output relative to quota as a policy act within +/-1000 kb/d; positive gaps above 100 kb/d for two consecutive months define the overproduction condition.
UAE unbound output choices are bounded between 3.4 and 4.85 mb/d reflecting its claimed capacity ceiling.
Forecast publications and public statements are zero-cost same-day messages visible to all actors.
Saudi surge actions reduce Gulf shut-in by 0.5 mb/d per month and credit the Saudi fiscal account as abstract revenue.
Waiting is a zero-cost available action for all actors.

Price dynamics: each month, Brent moves toward 60 USD/bbl at an assumed 6 USD/bbl per month when shut-ins normalize, and toward 110 USD/bbl at 4 USD/bbl per month when shut-ins persist above 3 mb/d; large baseline adoption adds a further assumed 8 USD/bbl downward step; these are conditional behavioral priors, not calibrated forecasts.
Monthly meeting windows for the seven adjusters recur on the first of each month; MOMR/OMR/STEO publication windows recur mid-month.

scheduledEvents.description: Monthly meeting of the seven voluntarily-adjusting members opens the adjust_monthly_quota decision window (recurs to 2027-06-01).
MSC assessment completion target; the Secretariat may table the assessment if completeness permits.
42nd ONOMM convenes; vote_baselines is executable only if the assessment was tabled, otherwise the baselines rule defaults to deferred.
Wider-alliance ~2 mb/d 2022-era cut layer and reaffirmed overall levels lapse unless the 42nd ONOMM outcome extends them.
MOMR/OMR/STEO publication window opens publish_forecast and updates compliance readings (recurs monthly to 2027-06-13).
Monthly Brent settlement update applying the conditional price dynamics of A19 based on the current shut-in and policy state (recurs to 2027-06-30).
Forecast horizon: terminal readout of in-force targets, baseline status, compliance gaps and the Brent June 2027 level.
